newsitem.title: USA: Oregon votes down one tax measure - reports.
newsitem.headline: Oregon votes down one tax measure - reports.

text.p: An Oregon ballot measure that would tighten requirements for tax measure approval appeared to headed for defeat on Tuesday, according to television reports.
Measure 46 would alter the debt issuance process in Oregon by redefining the voting majority to "all eligible" voters rather than, as it currently stands, all those who "participate" in a vote.
With 24 percent of precincts reporting, Measure 46 was opposed by 89 percent, with 11 percent in support, according to NorthWest Cable News.
Measure 32, which would permit the state to issue lottery revenue bonds for a light rail project, also appeared headed for defeat, with 54 percent opposed versus support of 46 percent.
The vote on Measure 47, which would limit property taxes, was too close to call, with the "no" vote narrowly ahead.
